title: answer --record leaves kb/_self/_decisions.csv uncommitted and the digest rewrites a tracked file, so the tick's next kbgit.py sync --push refuses and every later tick stalls
goal: `backlog.py answer --record` commits the decisions row it writes with the item file (a backlog-planning commit with its KB-Work trailer), and `kbdecide.py digest` writes the digest to an untracked or ignored path or commits it itself, so a manager tick's `kbgit.py sync --push` never refuses a tracked change the tick itself made; a test runs the sequence (answer --record, digest, sync --dry-run) in a throwaway clone and asserts a clean tree; found by the SP-itmjxudu review

run: set -e; d=$(mktemp -d); git clone -q "$PWD" "$d/r"; cd "$d/r"; f=$(grep -L '"sprint"' kb/_self/backlog/BG-*.json | head -1); id=$(basename "$f" .json); python3 _tools/backlog.py gate add "$id" --kind blocking --id g9 --question "Which colour?" --option a --option b --recommendation a --do "a=true" --do "b=true" >/dev/null; python3 _tools/backlog.py answer "$id" g9 --answer a --by autopilot --record >/dev/null; python3 _tools/backlog.py answer "$id" g9 --answer a --by operator >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; git add -A; git -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@example.com commit -qm "chore(backlog): gate" --no-verify; python3 _tools/backlog.py answer "$id" g9 --answer b --by operator --record >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; test -z "$(git status --porcelain)"

gates.question: Should kbdecide.py digest commit its file by default, or only with --commit?
